_note: Sitting Nebraska, South Dakota, Idaho, Montana, Alaska and Rhode Island state legislators, read on 2026-10-28 from the Open States current-legislator lists (compiled from each Legislature's own member pages). cmp-data.js carries a roster shell for every "rows" entry, and scripts/gen-district-boards.mjs opens a read-only board for each. Every chamber was full except Rhode Island House District 31, which is vacant: it has no row and no board, and the generator logs it as skipped. Seat spellings: Nebraska's one chamber is "LD n"; Alaska's Senate is lettered ("District A"–"District T", resolver keys 1–20); South Dakota's House is "District n", with 26A, 26B, 28A and 28B as single-member split seats (resolver keys 34–37) and every other district electing two members at large; Idaho's House is "LD n" with position 1 (Position A) or 2 (Position B), as listed. South Dakota names no seat within an at-large pair, so `position` 1 and 2 there are PolitiDex's numbering in roster order (sorted by surname), printed Seat A and Seat B, and marked positionAssignedBy: PolitiDex. Idaho Senator Mark Harris (harris_id) shares a display name with North Carolina's U.S. Rep. Mark Harris (mark_harris); the two are separate rows with separate ids. Nineteen members already carried an id in the app's stance files (state-senate-stances-w11.js, -w12.js and -w13.js: e.g. john_arch, kelly_anthon, bert_stedman); their shells use that id rather than a new one. Montana Rep. Becky Edwards (edwards_mt) is not Utah's Becky Edwards (becky_edwards).
